transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-16 15:00 PDT | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Ortiz (CSM), Tom Reilly (Mapleview CTO), Jared Lowe (Head of ML), Priya Nambiar (SRE), Alicia Gomez (Security), Rohit Varma (Platform)

Summary: quick run through of Console request/trace handoff, root-cause workflows, KV cache and fallback behavior, plus security queries around KMS and audit logs. Agreed to run a small hosted benchmark and share security pack.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining on a Thursday, we'll do a focused 45-ish minute runthrough of the console's incident paths and how your oncall can triage request failures. i'm Maya, i'm the AE. Samir on the line is our SE. Samir?

[00:12] Samir Patel: yeah hi all, i'll be walking through demos, specifically trace->request->payload replay and then how the fallback routing and model variants show up in the UI. quick note: audio might drop, sorry in advance for any weird transcrip.

[01:05] Tom Reilly: great to be here. our main ask is: we get intermittent 500s during peak batch periods on our payments pipeline and it's been opaque. we need a clean handoff to SREs and a reproducible replay path.

[01:30] Priya Nambiar: and we'd like to instrument KV cache misses and see whether fallback to a quantized variant is what actually causes latency spikes. also concerned about sensitive PII in logs, so need retention controls.

[02:02] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll share my screen — opening the console. first panel is the Request Inspector; you'll see a request timeline, then traces on the right, and request logs are down below.

[03:10] [Samir screen share audio low] Samir Patel: okay so here's a request where the runtime routed to a cheaper quantized v2; notice the model variant label in the top-left — we mark when a fallback happened and why (capacity vs cost policy). the trace links back to the node-level GPU queue times and also shows KV cache hit/miss events.

[05:20] Jared Lowe: can you show the raw request payload? I want to confirm if tokens are being prefetched or if our prompt templating expands unexpectedly. sometimes our preprocessor double-stuffs a JSON string.

[05:38] Samir Patel: yep clicking payload view — it's here. note the truncation policy, which we default to 'preserve_prompt' for safety, but you can change via per-route config. i can also toggle the KV cache overlay so you see which prefix segments were cached.

[07:00] Priya Nambiar: the timestamps on the trace look slightly shifted — is the trace clock synced to our infra? we've seen drift before.

[07:15] Samir Patel: good call. we ingest timestamps from the request agent plus GPU runtime metrics. there can be up to a couple second skew if the agent clock differs. we surface both the request timestamp and the runtime-timestamp to help correlate. we'll also show you a small helper to align them.

[09:02] Alicia Gomez: security question — where does the request log live? are logs written to S3 or to your managed store? encryption at rest and KMS integration are blockers for us.

[09:20] Maya Chen: short answer: for hosted we store in an encrypted store with customer-specific KMS keys; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS / HSM. we'll send the SOC2 + KMS integration docs.

[10:05] Tom Reilly: and retention — can we TTL at 30 days for request bodies but keep tokens/metadata for 180 days?

[10:22] Lina Ortiz: yes, retention is per-route; you can configure redaction rules too so PII fields are scrubbed before storage.

[11:10] [15:00] Samir Patel: moving on to failure triage — here's an example 500. the console shows an error summary, stack snippet from the runtime (best-effort), correlated downstream exception, and then a 'replay' button. when you hit replay we replay the exact request against a pinned model version in an isolated sandbox so you can reproduce without hitting production capacity.

[13:30] Rohit Varma: does replay use our data or is it synthetic? we can't have live PHI going into hosted sandboxes.

[13:45] Samir Patel: by default replay redacts PII using the configured redaction rules; you can also run replay in your VPC for Private deployments so data never leaves your network.

[15:00] Priya Nambiar: in one of our incidents, fallback routing routed to a larger model and caused a burst in token usage. can we see where a route policy bumped cost or changed routing?

[15:22] Samir Patel: yes — a routing decision block is captured in the trace. we show policy tags: latency_sla, cost_threshold, region_preference and the evaluated reason. here's a trace showing a policy-triggered fallback because the primary pool was at capacity; you can click into the autoscaling history to see why capacity didn't scale fast enough.

[17:55] Jared Lowe: can we get an alert if KV cache hit rate drops below X%?

[18:05] Samir Patel: absolutely — you can set SLA alerts on cache hit rate, latency p95, and a custom rule for fallback frequency. alerts can be routed to PagerDuty or Slack and include the trace link to jump straight into the inspector.

[20:00] [murmur / crosstalk] Speaker 1: (inaudible) -- oh, sorry, go ahead.

[21:15] Maya Chen: quick note on observability retention costs — we provide sampled request captures for high-volume routes so you don't store every token trace. Optimize suggests sampling rates based on cost vs debug value.

[22:30] Tom Reilly: on the pilot, we want the hosted route first to iterate fast but with VPC egress restrictions. is that possible?

[22:50] Maya Chen: yes you can start hosted with an IP allowlist and later migrate to Dedicated or Private. we also support per-tenant egress controls and can do a hybrid where only replays run inside your VPC.

[24:10] Alicia Gomez: one more security ask — audit logs for who replayed which request plus SAML SSO for RBAC scoping.

[24:30] Derek Ho: we capture audit events for all user actions in the console (replay, masking changes, rollouts). SSO with SAML/SCIM is supported and we can map roles to RBAC policies.

[26:00] [28:00] Samir Patel: demoing a real incident handoff now — opening the incident timeline. first step: triage notes (automatic), then run the 'replay in sandbox' and attach the sandbox id to the ticket. if the replay reproduces we can toggle a temporary route policy to fallback to a stable model while the devs fix the problem.

[29:40] Priya Nambiar: how often do automatic fallbacks trigger false positives? e.g., cache warmups that look like misses but are expected on cold starts.

[29:55] Samir Patel: we've got heuristics to detect cold-start patterns and suppress alerts for the initial minutes after deploy or autoscale events. you can tune sensitivity on those heuristics.

[32:10] Jared Lowe: wanted to ask about token accounting — sometimes we see token spikes that don't align with what we expect. will the request inspector attribute tokens to prompt vs completion and break down per-model?

[32:30] Samir Patel: yes the token ledger is broken down by prompt/completion/per-route and we show the model-specific per-token cost if you want. Optimize will also recommend quantization profiles if your workload is completion-heavy.

[34:00] Tom Reilly: on enterprise SLAs — if we move to Dedicated, what's the runbook for degraded GPU pool behavior? we need guaranteed fallback capacity.

[34:15] Maya Chen: Dedicated includes a reserved buffer and SLA-backed latency targets; plus we support automatic spillover to a cross-region pool or to a pinned higher-tier model set. we can include explicit fallback capacity in the contract.

[36:05] Alicia Gomez: compliance check — any certifications for EU data residency? we're multi-region EEA customers.

[36:20] Maya Chen: yes we support region pinning and can keep logs and request data in EEA regions. list of certifications (SOC2, ISO27001) will be in the pack we send.

[38:50] Samir Patel: quick walkthrough of a saved playbook — you can author triage steps (capture logs, run replay, toggle route policy) and attach them to JIRA or Zendesk. it's handy for rotating oncall teams.

[40:10] Rohit Varma: for the benchmark, we want to run our 10k token invoice extraction prompt and watch latency p50/p95 and token costs across three model variants (base, quantized, pinned fallback). can you configure that?

[40:25] Samir Patel: yes we'll create a benchmark job — hosted sandbox with sample prompts, KV cache enabled/disabled runs, and we'll produce a CSV with per-request traces and cost breakdown.

[42:00] Maya Chen: ok quick recap and next steps — i'll send security docs and retention/KMS notes; Samir will spin up the hosted benchmark and share access; Lina will coordinate pilot kickoff. Priya / Rohit to share sample request logs for replay.

[43:10] Tom Reilly: that's perfect. any blockers from our side? only sign-off from finance and security after they review the pack.

[43:30] Maya Chen: understood. we'll aim to get everything to you by Monday. thanks everyone.

[44:00] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: Several short audio drops, occasional mis-attributed speaker label (Speaker 1), minor transcription errors in technical terms (K V cache written separately, small punctuation issues).
